pnl_definition: Net trading revenue (NTR) of Jane Street Group, LLC and all affiliates globally: trading gains net of exchange, clearing, brokerage and financing costs, before compensation and other operating expenses. Calendar year, USD millions. From 2025 the reported NTR includes mark-to-market gains and losses on private and AI-company stakes (e.g. Anthropic, CoreWeave, Situational Awareness). Gross revenue (e.g. FT's $21.9bn for 2023) and adjusted EBITDA are excluded.
headcount_definition: Total firm employees worldwide (all offices). Year-end where a document-based count exists (2023: 2,631; 2024: 2,960). Other years are approximate year-end values interpolated from dated point-in-time snapshots (firm website, press). 2025 is a rounded 'about 3,500', and 2026 is an estimate as of mid-2026 (cutoff).
fx_note: Jane Street reports in USD; no FX conversion needed. India figures in INR (SEBI) and UK subsidiary accounts are excluded from the firm-wide series.
methodology: Rows for 2022-2026 rest on figures from Jane Street's bond offering documents and debt-investor disclosures, as relayed by Bloomberg, FT, Reuters and specialist trade press; the firm is private and publishes no accounts. 2020-2021 are bounded below by the FT's reading of the 2024 prospectus (NTR > $10bn in each of 2020-2023) and centred using Bloomberg's 12-months-to-March-2021 figure and an unverified Substack. 2015-2019 have no reported PnL and are scale-anchored estimates: US broker-dealer and firm-wide members' equity, headcount, the Q2 2019 ~$0.5bn chart reading, and market regime. Headcount combines document-based year-end counts (2023, 2024) with website, press and aggregator snapshots interpolated to year-end. Credible intervals follow the stated calibration: about ±2-3% for document-based press years, ±5-15% for bounded or single-source years, and ±50-100% for pre-2020 estimates.

entities.name: Jane Street (firm-wide)
entities.description: Jane Street Group, LLC consolidated with all trading affiliates worldwide (US, London, Hong Kong, Singapore, Amsterdam, India-linked entities). Subsidiary-only figures (Jane Street Capital LLC X-17A-5, Jane Street Europe Ltd, Jane Street UK Partnership LLP, India entities per SEBI) are context only and never used as firm-wide PnL.

rows.notes: No firm-wide revenue is reported for 2015. The PnL is a pure estimate anchored on scale. The US broker-dealer alone had $1.25bn of member's equity at end-2015 (X-17A-5; subsidiary balance sheet, not revenue). Firm-wide members' equity was about $2.1bn in 2016, derived from '$45bn, up nearly 2,000% since 2016'. Equity-to-NTR ran about 2x in 2023, which suggests NTR of roughly $1bn. The August 2015 ETF dislocation was a favourable volatility event. Headcount: about 500 in April 2015 (MIT Technology Review via Wikipedia), grown to an assumed ~550 by year-end. Bars are wide and asymmetric.

No reported PnL. Members' equity of about $2.1-2.3bn (derived) gives the scale. Reuters notes July 2026 was the 'first negative month since 2016', so 2016 had at least one losing month. Modest growth on 2015 is assumed (Brexit and US-election volatility). Headcount is interpolated between ~500 (Apr 2015) and ~750 (Aug 2018).

No reported PnL. 2017 was a historically low-volatility, lean year for market makers, so the estimate is flat to slightly down on 2016 despite headcount growth. Pure estimate with wide bars. Headcount is interpolated toward ~750 (website, Aug 2018).

No reported PnL. Volatility spikes (Feb 2018 'Volmageddon', Q4 2018 selloff) and continued ETF share gains suggest growth on 2017. Pure estimate. Headcount: about 750 per the firm website in Aug 2018 (via Wikipedia, low reliability), set at ~800 for year-end.

No calendar-2019 figure. Anchors disagree. (a) An X post reading a Bloomberg chart puts Q2 2019 NTR at ~$0.5bn, about $2-2.5bn annualised. (b) An unverified Substack says 2020 EBITDA jumped ~1,000%, implying low-single-digit-billion 2019 revenue. (c) Bloomberg's +54% to $10.6bn for the 12 months to Mar 2021 implies ~$6.9bn for Apr 2019-Mar 2020, but that window includes the extreme COVID Q1 2020 (likely ~$4-5bn alone). 2019 was a lean low-volatility year. The mid of $2.4bn is skewed high to allow for the LTM-based reading. Headcount is interpolated (website ~750 in 2018, ~900 snapshot possibly stale).

Lower bound from the FT reading of the 2024 prospectus: 2023 was the 'fourth straight year of NTR exceeding $10bn', so 2020 > $10bn. Bloomberg reported +54% to $10.6bn for the 12 months to March 2021 (non-calendar, via Wikipedia/MarketsWiki, net vs gross unclear). An unverified Substack gives FY2020 $11.4bn; its H1 2020 $8.4bn equals Bloomberg's H1 2024 figure, so it may be mis-dated. 2020 was an exceptionally strong volatile year (COVID, ETF/bond dislocations). Mid $11.0bn. The 'about 900' website figure (Aug 2020 Wikipedia, citing a 2018 access) looks stale, so year-end headcount is estimated at ~1,100.

Only a document-based lower bound: NTR > $10bn (FT, 2024 prospectus streak). No point figure. 2021 was a retail and crypto boom year; Q1 2021 (meme-stock volatility) fell inside Bloomberg's $10.6bn LTM to March 2021. Bloomberg later said 2023 was 'roughly flat' on 2022 ($10.7bn), and nothing suggests 2021 far exceeded 2022, so the upper bar is ~$13bn. Headcount: ~1,200 (website, May 2021) and 1,700+ (July 2022), so year-end ~1,400.

$10.7bn per Bloomberg (Jan 2024; figures disclosed to debt investors, people familiar; snippet only, not fetched). This is consistent with FT's >$10bn streak and Bloomberg's '2023 roughly flat'. The FT's +34% gross-revenue comparison implies 2022 GROSS revenue of ~$16.3bn. That is not the PnL metric and is excluded. Headcount: website 1,700+ (Jul 2022) and eFC/FT 'from 2,000 to 2,500' before Sep 2023, so year-end ~2,050.

NTR $10.5bn (FT Alphaville, from the April 2024 bond prospectus) and $10.6bn (Bloomberg). The difference is rounding; mid $10.55bn. TRAP RESOLVED: the FT's $21.9bn is explicitly GROSS revenue (before trading costs and interest; +34% YoY). The same article gives the $10.5bn net figure, so $21.9bn is excluded. Adjusted EBITDA was $7.4bn and comp $2.4bn. Headcount: 2,631 at 2023-12-31 per the prospectus (year-end), about $4.0m NTR per head. The Bloomberg 9M-2023 figure (~$7.0-7.3bn) implies Q4 of about $3.3bn.

NTR $20.5bn from the April 2025 bond offering documents, via Bloomberg, corroborated by FT and by The DESK's $6.9m NTR per employee (6.9 x 2,960 = $20.4bn). Quarterly build: Q1 $4.4bn (FT), H1 ~$8.4bn, 9M $14.2bn (Bloomberg), so Q4 ~$6.3bn. Net income $13bn per a Bloomberg relay (period not explicitly labelled there; consistent with FY). Members' equity $29.9bn. Headcount 2,960 at year-end 2024 (offering docs via Disruption Banking/eFC); The DESK implies ~2,970.

NTR $39.6bn per Bloomberg, independently Reuters. Quarters reconcile: Q1 ~$7.2bn (H1 $17.3bn less Q2), Q2 $10.1bn, Q3 $6.83bn, Q4 $15.5bn, summing to ~$39.6bn. The figure includes large mark-to-market gains on private and AI stakes (Anthropic, CoreWeave; ~$830m VC gains in Q3), so it is not pure market-making revenue. Adjusted EBITDA $31.2bn exceeds NTR less comp ($30.2bn), so it adds back some items and is not used. No FY2025 net income was reported (Q2 2025 net income was $6.9bn). Headcount ~3,500 (Bloomberg, 'only 3,500 employees'; consistent with the $9.4bn pay pool / $2.7m per head = ~3,480). This is a rounded, unlabelled figure; LinkedIn shows ~3,184-3,300 at end-2025. Treated as approximately year-end, with a ±7% band. TRAP: UK Companies House's $643m for 2025 is Jane Street Europe Ltd, a subsidiary/transfer-pricing entity, so it is excluded. UK LLP average staff grew 688 to 790 (+15%), consistent with firm-wide growth of ~15-18%.

Latest reliable figure: 'more than $40bn' of NTR year to date, including July's loss (Reuters, from people familiar plus a note to employees; FT says 'in the year to Friday', i.e. to 2026-08-14). Cutoff is 2026-07-31 because no August results were disclosed and the figure is the July month-end close revealed in the August refinancing. Q1 2026 was a record $16.1bn (Bloomberg and Reuters, with $10.3bn net income). July was about -$14-15bn (the refinancing disclosure says $14bn; FT/Reuters/WSJ say $15bn), the first negative month since 2016, driven by the Situational Awareness stake and AI-stock risk cuts. Reuters' 'down roughly 25% from the end-June peak' plus a $14-15bn July loss implies YTD of about $42-45bn (implied H1 ~$56-60bn, Q2 ~$40bn+). It also rules out reading the FT's $40bn as trailing-12-month. Mid $42bn. The low is set just under $40bn to allow for 'still $40bn' rounding. Q1-2026 TRAP RESOLVED: Hedgeweek's $27bn is Q1 2026 revenue COMBINED for Citadel Securities, Jane Street and HRT, not Jane Street alone, so there is no conflict with $16.1bn. Headcount: Reuters' boilerplate ~3,500 is likely carried over. Aggregators give 3,700-4,000 (Tracxn 3,865 at 2026-08-31), and the website says 'more than 3,000' (stale floor). Mid ~3,700 is derived from the ~15%/yr trend.

ytd_2026.description: The latest reliable firm-wide PnL is 'more than $40bn' of net trading revenue for 2026 to date, net of a ~$14-15bn July loss. Reuters and the FT reported it on 2026-08-14, based on the August 2026 bond-refinancing disclosure and a note to employees. Best estimate is ~$42bn (90% CI $39.5-46.5bn). The cutoff is the July 2026 month-end: Reuters explicitly says the figure includes July, no August data has been disclosed, and the FT's 'year to Friday' (2026-08-14) phrasing describes the same disclosure. Components: Q1 2026 $16.1bn (record); implied end-June peak ~$56-60bn; July ~-$14-15bn. No Q2, H1 or Q3 2026 figure has been reported. Headcount at cutoff is ~3,700 (range 3,450-4,000).

caveats: Jane Street is private. Every figure comes from debt-investor disclosures relayed by the press, often through syndications (Investing.com AI-assisted relays, Yahoo/GuruFocus, eFC) because Bloomberg/FT/WSJ bodies were paywalled. Several top-tier figures are confirmed only at headline or snippet level.
2015-2019 PnL values are scale-anchored estimates with no reported datapoint (2019 has only a social-media chart reading of Q2 ~$0.5bn). Do not treat them as data.

2020 and 2021 are bounded below at $10bn by the prospectus; mids are judgement. Bloomberg's $10.6bn (12 months to March 2021) is non-calendar, known only via Wikipedia/MarketsWiki, and numerically identical to FY2023's $10.6bn, a possible confusion risk.
The FT's $21.9bn for 2023 is GROSS revenue (and the derived ~$16.3bn for 2022 is gross too). Net trading revenue is roughly half of gross. These figures are excluded.

From 2025, NTR includes large investment marks (Anthropic, CoreWeave, Situational Awareness), so 2025-2026 PnL is more volatile and less comparable with earlier market-making-only years. July 2026 alone was about -$14-15bn.

The Hedgeweek $27bn Q1 2026 figure is a three-firm combined total (Citadel Securities + Jane Street + HRT), not a Jane Street number. UK Companies House figures ($643m Jane Street Europe revenue; 790 UK LLP staff) and SEBI India figures are subsidiary-only.

Circular sourcing: many 2025-2026 trade-press items (eFC, Hedgeweek, GuruFocus, Wikipedia) restate the same Bloomberg/Reuters/FT line and are not independent corroboration. Bloomberg and Reuters are treated as the independent pair.

Headcount before 2023 comes from firm-website snapshots transcribed on Wikipedia, which may be stale (e.g. ~900 in 2020 cites a 2018 access). The 2025 '3,500' is rounded and unlabelled (year-end vs average). The 2026 headcount relies partly on aggregators.

H1/Q2 2026 NTR and August-September 2026 results; the August 2026 offering memo was not obtained. Is the July loss $14bn or $15bn?
FY2025 net income and whether the 2025 '3,500 employees' is year-end or average.
